set: English Drill 1: Grammar in the 2026 pattern

sections.name: English drill: Grammar in the 2026 pattern

questions.q: Choose the correct inverted structure:
opts: Under no circumstances did the patient should be left alone.
Under no circumstances the patient should be left alone.
Under no circumstances should the patient be left alone.
Under no circumstances should be left the patient alone.
questions.why: Negative phrase at the start: auxiliary + subject. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct option: “Scarcely had I reached home ______ it started raining.”
questions.why: 'Scarcely … when'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct option: “I would rather you ______ the report today.”
questions.why: 'Would rather' + another subject takes the past form. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct conditional sentence:
opts: If I had known about the strike, I will have stayed at home.
Had I knew about the strike, I would have stayed at home.
Had I known about the strike, I would stay at home yesterday.
Had I known about the strike, I would have stayed at home.
questions.why: 'Had I known' = 'If I had known' (third conditional). GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence:
opts: He is more taller than I.
He is taller than me am.
questions.why: After 'than', 'I' (as in 'than I am') is the formal correct form; GPSC keys follow this. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the error: “Bread and butter are his daily breakfast.”
questions.why: Two nouns that name one thing take a singular verb: 'is'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Find the error: “The number of patients have increased this month.”
questions.why: 'The number of' is singular ('has'); 'a number of' is plural. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the error: “She has went to the dispensary.”
questions.why: After 'has', use the past participle: 'has gone'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Spot the error: “She is senior than me by two years.”
questions.why: 'Senior', 'junior', 'superior', 'inferior' take 'to': 'senior to me'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the error: “Mathematics are taught by Mr Naik.”
questions.why: Subject names ending in -ics take a singular verb: 'is taught'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “The nurse is dressing the wound.”
opts: The wound is being dressed by the nurse.
The wound was being dressed by the nurse.
The wound is been dressed by the nurse.
The wound is dressed by the nurse.
questions.why: Present continuous passive: is being + past participle. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “You must follow these rules.”
questions.why: Modal passive: modal + be + past participle. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Select the correct indirect speech: He said, “I will come tomorrow.”
opts: He said that I would come the next day.
He said that he would come the next day.
He said that he would come yesterday.
He said that he will come tomorrow.
questions.why: will → would; tomorrow → the next day. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Select the correct indirect speech: She said, “What a beautiful garden!”
opts: She said what a beautiful garden it was!
She asked that it was a beautiful garden.
She exclaimed that what a beautiful garden.
She exclaimed that it was a very beautiful garden.
questions.why: Exclamations become 'exclaimed that … very …'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct transformation: “No other city in India is as large as Mumbai.” (comparative degree)
opts: Mumbai is larger than any other city in India.
Mumbai is the largest than other cities in India.
Mumbai is larger than any city in India.
Mumbai is as large as any other city in India.
questions.why: Positive → comparative with 'any other'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “I ______ for an hour when the doctor finally called me.”
questions.why: A continuing action up to a point in the past: past perfect continuous. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct modal: “You ______ not park here; it is a no-parking zone.”
questions.why: 'Must not' = prohibition. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “Water ______ at 100 °C at sea level.”
questions.why: Universal truths take the simple present. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct modal: “She ______ have reached by now; she left two hours ago.”
questions.why: 'Should have' for an expected result. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “He ______ the files when the auditor walked in.”
questions.why: An action in progress interrupted by another: past continuous. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the clause type: “I know that he is innocent.”
questions.why: 'That he is innocent' is the object of 'know'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the clause type: “We left before the storm broke.”
questions.why: 'Before the storm broke' tells when. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct preposition: “The medicine is good ______ cough.”
questions.why: 'Good for' (beneficial); 'good at' (skilled). GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct preposition: “He prevented me ______ going out.”
questions.why: 'Prevent from'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the conjunction relationship: “He was tired, so he went to bed early.”
questions.why: 'So' introduces a result. GPSC-style practice item.
